paraphrase: Seeking the qualities that make a Buddha, Sumedha discerns the ten perfections one after another — giving, virtue, renunciation, wisdom, energy, patience, truthfulness, determination, loving-kindness and equanimity — each with a simile (an overturned water-jar, a yak guarding its tail, a prisoner leaving jail, a monk begging from every house, a lion, the earth that bears all, the morning star keeping its course, a rocky mountain unmoved by wind, water cooling good and bad alike, the earth indifferent to what is thrown on it), and resolves to fulfil them.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked). Similes summarised from memory of the Buddhavaṃsa and checked only for the section range; order and names of the ten perfections confirmed in the local text (bv2:116–161).

paraphrase: The ascetic Sumedha lays himself face down in the mud so that the Buddha Dīpaṅkara and his monks may walk over him; he reflects that he could realise the Dhamma then and there but will rather attain omniscience and carry the world across on the ship of Dhamma; eight conditions make the aspiration succeed (human birth, the male sex, the cause, seeing a teacher, going forth, attainment of qualities, an act of devotion and strong desire); Dīpaṅkara, standing at his head, declares that after countless aeons he will be the Buddha Gotama.
notes: Sutta id and segment range checked in the local bilara-data copy (Mahāsaṅgīti root text, read alongside Sujato's CC0 English); paraphrase by U36 (skeleton phase, fidelity not yet checked). Recorded faithfully: the male sex (liṅgasampatti) is listed among the eight conditions for the aspiration to Buddhahood (Bv 2.59).

paraphrase: Human birth, the (male) sex, the cause, seeing the Teacher, going forth, attainment of qualities, an act of devotion and desire: by the combination of these eight things the aspiration succeeds.

original.text: Manussattaṁ liṅgasampatti, hetu satthāradassanaṁ; Pabbajjā guṇasampatti, adhikāro ca chandatā; Aṭṭhadhammasamodhānā, abhinīhāro samijjhati’.
